result:
No actions this turn. I've already read the repo, so I'll reply.

---

Here's what I understand: you want the timetable site to warn visitors when a sailing has been cancelled, so they don't turn up for a boat that isn't running.

Here's how it works today. The Flask app reads `sailings.csv`, which the ferry office exports each night, and renders it into `timetable.html`. Nothing in that CSV says whether a sailing is cancelled, and the site has no warning code yet.

That leads to something that will shape the whole design: **the site has no way to know about a cancellation right now.** Someone or something has to tell it. Because the data arrives once a night, it also couldn't pick up a sailing cancelled in the morning for that afternoon unless a new source or update path is added. Cancellations often happen at short notice, for weather or breakdowns, so that gap may matter a lot.

Correct me if I've got any of that wrong.

What's prompting this now? I'd like to hear what happened, or what you want to stop happening, when someone checks the timetable and a sailing is off.
